h: Timing Your Visit and Exploring the Helford
p: Grey seals around the Cornish coast mostly give birth in the autumn and early winter, and that's when the hospital is at its busiest with orphaned and injured pups arriving. Visiting at that time of year can be a real eye-opener, as you're seeing rescue work in full swing. In summer, the focus shifts to the permanent residents and to pups that are close to going home, so whichever season you choose, there's something different going on.

Alongside the seals, the sanctuary has been home to other rescued and resident animals over the years, and the keepers' talks explain how each one came to be there. Kids often come away wanting to know what they can do to help, and picking up litter on the next beach visit is a lovely place to start.

Gweek sits at the very head of the Helford River, one of Cornwall's most beautiful wooded estuaries. Further down the river, the subtropical gardens at Trebah and Glendurgan run steeply down to little beaches, and Glendurgan has a famous cherry laurel maze that children love getting lost in.

Head south onto the Lizard peninsula and you'll reach Lizard Point, the most southerly point of mainland Britain, with dramatic cliffs and a lighthouse. Kynance Cove, with its turquoise water and serpentine rocks, is a showstopper. Helston, the nearest market town, is home to the Flambards theme park, a handy option for families wanting rides after a gentler morning.
